s: JWT, OAuth2, sessions, RBAC, SSO, MFA
d: Auth is two questions: 'Who are you?' (authentication) and 'What can you do?' (authorization). JWTs, OAuth2 flows, session management, and role-based access control are daily concerns. One bad implementation can expose all user data.
c: OAuth2 flows (Authorization Code, Client Credentials, PKCE)

p: Authentication verifies WHO a user is. Authorization verifies WHAT they are allowed to do. Modern backends typically use JWT (JSON Web Tokens) or session cookies for stateless/stateful authentication.
2. Server hashes password (bcrypt) and compares to DB.
3. Server generates a signed JWT or Session ID.
4. Client sends Token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on subsequent requests.

// Generating a JWT
const token = jwt.sign(
  { userId: user.id, role: user.role }, 
  process.env.SECRET_KEY, 
  { expiresIn: '1h' }
);

[Client] --(username, pw)--> [Server]
[Client] <--(signed JWT)-- [Server]

[Client] --(GET /data + JWT)--> [Server validates signature]
[Client] <--(Secure Data)-- [Server]
